title: Gathering up, and Optional for no answer

terminal.description: A shell in your workspace. Run the season report here, and try your types from main.

tasks.title: Add up the season's seats
tasks.description:
Under `// Task 1`, write a class `Totals` with three methods, each one stream from `bookings` to its answer. `static int seats(List<Booking> bookings)` gives back all the seats booked, added up. `static double average(List<Booking> bookings)` gives back the seats of a booking on average, and 0 when there are no bookings. `static int most(List<Booking> bookings)` gives back the most seats in one booking, and 0 when there are no bookings. `Booking` is given above the tasks.

Check hands each method lists of its own: one whose average is not a whole number, one booking, and none. Its list refuses to be read by a loop, `get`, `forEach` or a copy, so only a stream can read it. Check reads what comes back, and the list afterwards.
nextSteps: Read the part of the lesson about streams of numbers.
Turn the stream of bookings into a stream of their seats.
Finish it with the ending each method asks for.
For average and most, say what to give back when there are no bookings.
hints: A stream of bookings has no sum, average or largest: those belong to a stream of plain numbers, which a stream of objects can become.

One step turns each booking into an int and gives a stream of ints. Its average and its largest may not exist, so they come back in a box that may be empty, and the box can be asked for a value to use when it is empty.

tasks.title: Count the bookings per boat, and write the names in a line
tasks.description:
Under `// Task 2`, write a class `Season` with two methods, each one stream from `bookings` to its answer. `static Map<String, Long> bookingsPerBoat(List<Booking> bookings)` gives back a map from each boat to the number of its bookings. `static String namesLine(List<Booking> bookings)` gives back the passengers in the order they came, with a comma and a space between two names, as in `Ishbel, Torquil`, and nothing at either end.

Check hands both methods lists of its own that only a stream can read, as in Task 1: several boats mixed, one booking, and none. It compares the map with the right one as a map, whatever order it keeps, and reads the line letter by letter, and the list afterwards.
nextSteps: Read the part of the lesson about collect, groupingBy and joining.
Write bookingsPerBoat: gather the bookings into groups by boat, and count each group.
Write namesLine: turn each booking into its passenger, and join the names.
hints: One ending gathers a stream into something other than a list, and Java has a class of ready-made gatherers to hand it: a map of groups, a count, a line of text.

One collector sorts things into a map by a key, and can be handed a second collector for what each group becomes; counting a group gives a long. Another joins texts with what you put between them, and nothing at the ends.

videos.title: Grouping a stream into a map

tasks.title: Answer when there may be no answer
tasks.description:
Under `// Task 3`, write a class `Lookup` with two methods. `static Optional<Booking> largestOn(List<Booking> bookings, String boat)` gives back the booking with most seats on that boat, or an empty `Optional` when that boat has none. `static String firstOn(List<Booking> bookings, String boat)` gives back the passenger of the first booking on that boat, or `"nobody"` when it has none. A stream makes each one short; a loop that gives the same answers passes too.

Check calls both with lists of its own, for boats with bookings, a boat with none, and an empty list. It reads the `Optional` that comes back as a value: a booking in it, or empty, and never `null`. Asking an empty one for its value is a mistake Check names.
nextSteps: Read the part of the lesson about Optional.
Write largestOn: keep the boat's bookings, and ask for the largest by seats.
Write firstOn: keep the boat's bookings, take the first, turn it into its passenger.
Say what firstOn gives back when there is no first booking.
hints: Some stream endings give back an Optional, because there may be no answer: the largest, the first. An Optional can be given back as it is, or asked what to do when it is empty.

The largest needs a Comparator, as sorting does. An Optional can turn what is in it into something else, and stay empty when it is empty, and give a value of your own when it is empty. Asking an empty one for its value with get throws.
